why: Both migrations are the same correct one-line wrap of the single shared AsyncOpenAI client with equivalent verification, so the decision rests on system judgment, where B spans scales — quick wins (cache key, retry predicate), changes (per-agent labels keyed off the existing [llm.*] config names, host unlock), rework (deleting app/bedrock.py's 334-line hand-rolled converse translation in favour of BYOK catalog ids, moving the VMind call off axios) and an account-level spend cap for an unbounded autonomous loop — with correct Router mechanics throughout (fallbacks forfeit Flex, no fallback mid-stream, truncated attempts billed, a capped key 401s and so composes with the retry fix). A's three branches are each better measured and better reasoned per item, and its vision-catalog fix is the single best improvement either engineer shipped, but A stops at migration tune-up scale: no spend caps, nothing at rework scale, and model choice deferred wholesale to the human. Neither engineer reached the real bar — neither asked whether any of these calls should exist (the chart-insight and planning calls, a smaller model for the vision step, per-feature model tiering), and neither touched shadow models, Jev or Switchyard.
A_best: It found and fixed the one staleness Router cannot paper over: MULTIMODAL_MODELS is six names from 2024, so a browser agent's screenshots were being silently stripped on every current model (ask_with_images raised outright) — derived from the catalog's per-model image support, measured before/after on sonnet-5, haiku-4-5 and gpt-5.4-mini, and confirmed live. It also moved more real traffic, generalising the host unlock to whatever endpoint the deployment configured while excluding loopback and private ranges as a residency boundary, and chose claude-sonnet-4-6 over the cheaper sonnet-5 for the 3.7 map because sonnet-5's entry rejects temperature and the examples' temperature=0.0 would have been dropped — the sharper call on exactly the decision B got looser.
B_best: It caught the defect A missed entirely: all three entry points retried on bare `Exception` six times with up to 60s backoff, so a provider rejection became six Router requests (measured: 6 requests/13s → 1 request/1.4s), multiplied by a 20-step loop, pressing against a spend cap enforced after usage is recorded — and it tied that to the cap proposal and to Router's 429/504 surface. Its per-agent spend labels turn a config structure the class already had and threw away into both attribution and per-agent policy granularity, and it diagnosed the untouchable chart path precisely (VMind 2.0.5 uses axios, which in node bypasses the fetch the TS runtime wraps) rather than just declaring it out of reach.
A_worst: Everything stays at migration scale: no spend cap on a key driving an autonomous loop with max_input_tokens unset in every shipped example, no rework-level proposal at all (the fragile bedrock.py translation with its module-global CURRENT_TOOLUSE_ID is only a 'stays' plus a pricing note), and the biggest lever — which model serves which feature — handed back as decision d1 with a price table rather than a recommendation. It never noticed the retry storm sitting on the hot path it was labelling and timing out.
B_worst: It saw the stale MULTIMODAL_MODELS whitelist — its own i4 evidence notes the image path fails because no 3.7 Sonnet id is listed — and left it as a footnote on another item instead of fixing the bug that blinds a browser agent. Its i4 also bundles the host unlock with a 3.7→sonnet-5 swap, so the shipped default configuration routes only if a human accepts a model and sampling change at once, and provider_timeout for the two entry points with no timeout at all was left proposed rather than built.
